```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea A's core feature is given away free by funded competitors (Kintsugi, Numeral, TaxJar), according to A's own brief. A paid standalone monitor is competing against $0 for the same function. Idea B also faces free tiers, but its brief shows paid tiers selling at $29-100/mo from several live, small-team competitors (Kick, FlexedLedger, Finlens's $49 AI tier). That gives B a sourced price anchor for self-serve payment.",
    "A has a documented substitute that removes the problem entirely. Founders move to a Merchant of Record (Paddle, Lemon Squeezy) rather than pay for a tool that only flags exposure. A's addressable segment is therefore founders with cross-border revenue near a threshold who are not on a Merchant of Record. The brief leaves that segment's size as an open question. B's need, reconciling Stripe and bank feeds into usable books, applies to every Stripe-connected solo founder.",
    "B's demand evidence is broader and more concrete. It cites three independent sources, including a quantified time cost of 3-4 hours a month and a founder who pays a bookkeeper despite the expense. A has two sources, one from 2020 and one a single blog post. The 2025 end of A's claimed '2020-2025' span is not shown in the quotes.",
    "B names a low-cost channel aimed directly at the target user, the Stripe App Marketplace, alongside Indie Hackers and Reddit threads where the pain is already being discussed. A's cheap channel is newsletter sponsorship, backed by one anecdote. A's SEO route runs into funded competitors' existing content.",
    "B's narrower wedge, pure Stripe-to-bank reconciliation (raised in its open questions), is mechanical and rules-based, which suits a solo operator with agents. A's lean build, by contrast, still carries liability and ongoing upkeep of jurisdiction threshold data, with no revenue mechanism beyond what free tools already offer."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's main proof that a monitoring-only product can charge $49/mo is Tax Threshold Radar. The brief admits its testimonials could not be verified and that it may be an unvalidated landing page on a vercel.app domain. Without it, A has no sourced evidence that anyone pays for standalone monitoring. Quaderno is only an adjacent product.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence; this is a close call between two crowded spaces with free competitors. B carries real risks its brief flags: SOC2 and trust expectations, more than six competitors, finance-keyword ad costs that can exceed $50/click, and no clear differentiation as written. B also has thin spots. The Growthy $400-600/mo bookkeeper-time figure has no link and is effectively unsourced, and its GDPR/CCPA specifics are marked [unsourced], so neither was given weight. B wins mainly because A's pain has a free solution and a structural substitute, both documented in A's own brief, while B shows sourced evidence that small self-serve tools collect recurring fees."
}
```
